title: Agents Need Feature Flags - Sachin Gupta
talk_summary: Sachin Gupta argues agents need the same release discipline as web services (canaries, segments, kill switches) but across six agent-specific behavior surfaces: prompts, tools, models, memory, autonomy, and subagents. He proposes a middleware flag layer that every agent and subagent must route through, plus a rollout playbook and four metrics.

takeaways.technique: Agent-wide and per-tool kill switch in middleware
takeaways.what_they_do: A pre-wired off switch resolved per decision point (not per session) that halts inflight agents gracefully within seconds without deploy or restart.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every inflight agent process sees the flag at its next decision point. Each one emit a graceful shutdown
takeaways.numbers: 30 seconds from problem to mitigation; target time-to-mitigation under 5 minutes

takeaways.what_they_do: Route traffic by segment to different models and flip to a stable fallback on outage/deprecation without code changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a model routing flag is the difference between flipping a switch and shipping a hot fix in the middle of an incident

takeaways.what_they_do: Move system prompts out of code into flag-resolved config; roll new prompt to a small cohort and promote only if error rate holds.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Move the system prompt out of the code and into a flag resolve config
takeaways.numbers: block promotion if error rate climbs more than 2% over baseline at 5% rollout

takeaways.technique: Tool access flags per segment/risk class
takeaways.what_they_do: Tool existence is separate from authorization; gate money-moving, data-deleting, or compliance-sensitive tools per user tier or risk class.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The tool exists in your codebase whether the agent can call it. It is the flag.

takeaways.what_they_do: All spawned child agents must route model/tool/autonomy calls through the same flag middleware as the parent, so kill switches and routing reach them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sub agents must go through the same middleware

takeaways.what_they_do: Default new surfaces to suggest, promote to auto-approve per surface as trust builds, and make auto-execute opt-in per tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Default everything to suggest. Auto approve per surface as you build trust. Auto execute is optin per tool.
